title: Stop the register endpoint from making admins
summary: Registration passes $request->all() straight to create(), so is_admin goes through. Close it with $fillable and validated input.

files.content:
<?php

namespace App\Http\Controllers\Auth;

use App\Http\Controllers\Controller;
use App\Models\User;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;

class RegisterController extends Controller
{
    public function store(Request $request)
    {
        $user = User::create($request->all());

        return response()->json($user, 201);
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Models;

use Illuminate\Foundation\Auth\User as Authenticatable;

class User extends Authenticatable
{
    protected $guarded = [];

    protected $hidden = ['password', 'remember_token'];

    protected function casts(): array
    {
        return [
            'is_admin' => 'boolean',
            'password' => 'hashed',
        ];
    }
}

turns.user: someone reported they posted is_admin=1 to the register api and got an admin account. seriously??

assistant.body: Great catch! Two things line up here. $request->all() passes every field that was sent, and $guarded = [] on User accepts every one of them. In other words, anyone who adds is_admin to the request is an admin. $fillable decides which columns are accepted, and the controller only passes what survived validation.

turns.user: wait the admin panel has a toggle for is_admin. does that break now

assistant.body: Yes, as it stands it stops working. is_admin is not in $fillable, so create() and update() drop it silently without an error. The key point: use forceFill() only on the route that admins alone can reach, and name the column there. The route's authorization is what keeps ordinary input away from it.
